label: Aviation - FBOs, MRO, Airports
lead_task: Remove hydraulic fluid, grease, and exhaust soil from ground-support equipment and approved aircraft-adjacent components.
asset: Ground-support equipment, shop floors, wheel-well tooling, engine stands, and approved aluminum or coated parts
soil: Hydraulic oil, lubricating grease, carbon film, rubber transfer, and ramp grime
method: Low-pressure pre-rinse, controlled degreasing, manual agitation, and a complete rinse
concentration: Use only the current CR HD or Neutral label/TDS range; begin at the weakest effective dilution after an aluminum, coating, and elastomer coupon test.
process: Record solution temperature, wet dwell, brush or parts-washer agitation, rinse-water quality, and dry time; never let chemistry dry on the surface.
boundary: Use the operator's maintenance manual, material approvals, lockout, FOD controls, and wash-water capture. No application to flight-critical parts without written engineering approval.
verification: Dry visual inspection under task lighting, white-wipe or water-break check where approved, and corrosion/coating inspection before return to service.
materials: Aluminum alloy, stainless steel, painted steel, composites, sealants, and elastomers
wastewater: Capture ramp and shop wash water; route oil-bearing waste through the airport's approved separator and discharge program.

label: Breweries, Distilleries & Wineries
lead_task: Run an alkaline-and-acid CIP sequence against organic film, beer stone, and mineral scale in process circuits.
asset: Fermenters, bright tanks, kettles, fillers, kegs, transfer lines, and plate heat exchangers
soil: Krausen, protein, carbohydrate film, yeast, beer stone, tartrate, and mineral scale
method: Validated CIP: pre-rinse, alkaline circulation, intermediate rinse, acid circulation when required, final rinse, then the site's sanitation step
concentration: Current CIP directions use 0.5–1.5 L per 10 gal; select within that range from soil load, circuit volume, temperature, and a witnessed trial.
process: Log make-up concentration, return temperature, turbulent flow, circulation time, conductivity, rinse pH, and visual condition at the return.
boundary: Isolate the circuit, verify 316 stainless/PVC/gasket compatibility, prevent cross-connections, and keep cleaning separate from the facility's validated sanitizing step.
verification: Rinse-return pH and conductivity at baseline, no visible soil at inspection points, plus the plant's ATP, allergen, or microbiological release test.
materials: 316 stainless steel, PVC, approved hoses, pump seals, valve seats, and heat-exchanger gaskets
wastewater: Neutralize and discharge only within the site's pretreatment permit, pH limits, organic loading controls, and volume schedule.

label: Construction
lead_task: Clean concrete-handling equipment, forms, tools, and fleet assets without spreading silica-bearing solids or oily wash water.
asset: Concrete pumps, forms, mixers, hand tools, compact equipment, vehicle exteriors, and finished masonry
soil: Cement film, form oil, hydraulic grease, asphalt transfer, rust, and mineral efflorescence
method: Dry removal first, then targeted wet cleaning, agitation, and contained low-pressure rinse
concentration: Choose the weakest current-label dilution that removes the identified cement, oil, or mineral soil after a hidden-area compatibility test.
process: Record surface temperature, controlled wet dwell, brush or low-pressure agitation, and rinse volume; prevent mist and never dry-grind a chemical-cleaning residue.
boundary: Follow silica controls, equipment OEM limits, coating compatibility, stormwater plans, and site containment. Do not acid-clean uncured or architecturally sensitive concrete without approval.
verification: No visible cement or oily film, clean white-wipe where practical, acceptable finish in the test area, and documented wash-water recovery.
materials: Carbon steel, aluminum, hydraulic seals, painted equipment, cured concrete, masonry, and form coatings
wastewater: Collect slurry and wash water; settle solids and route liquid under the site's SWPPP and local discharge authorization.

label: Data Centers
lead_task: Restore heat-transfer performance in isolated cooling-water assets while keeping chemistry away from energized IT space.
asset: Cooling towers, plate heat exchangers, condenser-water piping, closed loops, strainers, and mechanical-room coils
soil: Carbonate scale, iron oxide, corrosion product, silt, and water-side organic fouling
method: Isolated side-stream or recirculating clean, controlled rinse, and documented water-treatment restart
concentration: Set descaler concentration from the current label/user guide, deposit analysis, metallurgy, and loop volume; water-treatment dose remains site-engineered.
process: Trend inlet/return temperature, flow, pressure drop, solution pH, iron or hardness response, contact time, agitation/recirculation, and rinse conductivity.
boundary: Use MOP/SOP/EOP change control, redundancy approval, leak containment, LOTO, and zero open chemical work above live electrical or IT equipment.
verification: Recovered approach temperature or pressure drop, stable rinse pH/conductivity, clean strainer inspection, and no leak or alarm after controlled restart.
materials: Copper, stainless steel, carbon steel, aluminum coils, elastomers, treatment probes, and coated tower components
wastewater: Capture spent cleanout solution; characterize metals and pH before routing through the facility's approved wastewater path.

label: Distribution / Cold Storage
lead_task: Remove forklift oil, tire marks, food soils, and mineral buildup without leaving a slippery film in an operating facility.
asset: Warehouse floors, loading docks, forklifts, battery areas, drains, cold-room surfaces, and isolated evaporator components
soil: Hydraulic oil, tire polymer, pallet grime, food residue, ice-related mineral scale, and drain film
method: Sweep or scrape, pre-treat, low-foam auto-scrub or controlled foam, recover, and rinse
concentration: Use the current low-foam or general-cleaning label range; start weak, increase only after a slip-residue and coating test.
process: Log floor temperature, dilution, wet dwell, pad/brush agitation, recovery passes, final rinse, and dry-to-traffic time.
boundary: Segregate food and packaging, isolate traffic and powered equipment, follow freezer/OEM limits, and do not represent cleaning as sanitizing.
verification: No visible oil or tire film, dry white-wipe, facility slip-resistance check, clear drains, and release only after the floor is dry.
materials: Sealed concrete, epoxy, urethane, rubber tires, painted steel, stainless steel, aluminum, and drain components
wastewater: Recover scrubber solution; route grease and solids through the site's interceptor, pretreatment, and discharge schedule.

label: Drone Cleaning Companies
lead_task: Deliver low-pressure exterior cleaning from a drone while controlling overspray, runoff, and finish compatibility.
asset: Roofs, façades, siding, glazing, solar modules, canopies, and elevated coated surfaces
soil: Atmospheric soot, algae and mildew staining, bird residue, salt film, and loose particulate
method: Ground-tested chemistry, calibrated low-pressure spray, controlled dwell, and rinse only where the label and substrate require it
concentration: Use the weakest current-label dilution that passes a ground-level finish and runoff test; never increase concentration to compensate for poor coverage.
process: Record ambient/surface temperature, wind, nozzle flow, application rate, dwell, any rinse pass, flight path, and treated area.
boundary: Follow aircraft and spray-system OEM limits, aviation rules, exclusion zones, overspray controls, landscaping protection, and electrical clearances.
verification: Matched-angle before/after images after drying, no streak or residue, coating/gloss check, and complete runoff-capture record.
materials: Coated metal, glass, roofing membrane, painted masonry, sealants, photovoltaic coatings, and landscaping
wastewater: Map drainage before flight; block storm inlets and capture or divert runoff under the property permit.

label: Education
lead_task: Clean campus mechanical, kitchen, restroom, and exterior assets within occupied-building and school-calendar controls.
asset: Boilers, cooling towers, heat exchangers, kitchen equipment, restroom fixtures, gym floors, drains, and hardscape
soil: Mineral scale, rust, grease, soap film, tracked soil, algae staining, and drain residue
method: Zone-specific descaling, degreasing, or surface cleaning during approved work windows
concentration: Use the applicable current label/TDS range and approve the starting dilution through facilities, EHS, and a small-area trial.
process: Document solution/surface temperature, dwell, agitation, rinse, ventilation, barricade time, and dry/reoccupancy release.
boundary: Schedule around students, isolate ventilation and traffic, protect food service, and keep cleaning distinct from district-approved disinfection.
verification: Visual and white-wipe acceptance, neutral rinse where applicable, no slip residue, and mechanical performance trend for water-side work.
materials: Stainless steel, copper, carbon steel, resilient flooring, sealed concrete, ceramic, grout, paint, and elastomers
wastewater: Route kitchen grease, scale-bearing cleanout, and floor solution through district-approved pretreatment and local sewer rules.

label: Fleet, Trucking & Car Washes
lead_task: Remove road film, bugs, grease, and aluminum oxidation without damaging fleet finishes or wash-bay controls.
asset: Truck and bus exteriors, wheels, aluminum tanks, chassis, engine bays, wash-bay floors, and service equipment
soil: Road film, insect residue, diesel soot, lubricating grease, brake dust, salt, and aluminum oxidation
method: Cool-surface pre-rinse, task-specific wash or degrease, soft agitation, complete rinse, and controlled dry
concentration: Stay within the current wash/degreaser label range and establish a separate tested ratio for aluminum brightening; start with the weakest effective solution.
process: Record water hardness, solution and panel temperature, dwell, brush or pressure agitation, rinse volume, and drying conditions.
boundary: Keep chemistry off hot panels, brakes, sensors, polished finishes, and unapproved aluminum; follow fleet OEM and wash-equipment limits.
verification: No road or oily film, no streaking after dry, gloss/finish acceptance, clean wheel test area, and no oily sheen in recovered water.
materials: Clear coat, painted steel, aluminum, stainless steel, chrome, rubber, plastics, glass, and sensor housings
wastewater: Use oil-water separation and solids capture; discharge only through the wash bay's permitted reclaim or sewer route.

label: Food & Beverage
lead_task: Validate a CIP or COP cleaning sequence against product soil and mineral deposit before the separate sanitation release.
asset: Process tanks, piping, fillers, pasteurizers, heat exchangers, kettles, conveyors, and removable parts
soil: Fat, protein, carbohydrate, yeast, biofilm-supporting residue, beer or milk stone, and hard-water scale
method: Pre-rinse, alkaline cleaning, intermediate rinse, acid step where required, final rinse, inspection, then the plant's sanitation process
concentration: For the published CR/HCR CIP use, select 0.5–1.5 L per 10 gal from soil load and trial evidence; other products remain within their current labels.
process: Log make-up concentration, temperature, turbulent flow or mechanical action, dwell/circulation time, conductivity, return condition, and final rinse pH.
boundary: Use the facility SSOP, isolate product and allergen paths, verify food-contact materials, and never substitute a cleaning claim for sanitizing or disinfection.
verification: No visible residue, rinse pH/conductivity at baseline, and the facility's ATP, protein/allergen, or microbiological acceptance result.
materials: 304/316 stainless steel, PVC, approved elastomers, conveyor polymers, aluminum where permitted, and heat-exchanger gaskets
wastewater: Balance pH and organic load within the pretreatment permit; schedule discharge volume with the plant's wastewater operator.

label: Food Processing & Agriculture
lead_task: Remove organic process soil and mineral film from plant or farm equipment before the site's sanitation or biosecurity step.
asset: Process vessels, lines, harvest equipment, bins, conveyors, wash-down areas, milking or beverage components, and drains
soil: Fat, protein, starch, sugar, plant residue, fertilizer salt, manure-adjacent soil, and hard-water scale
method: Dry pickup where possible, controlled COP/CIP or foam clean, agitation, full rinse, inspection, then the approved sanitation step
concentration: Use 0.5–1.5 L per 10 gal only for the applicable CR/HCR CIP direction; all other tasks require the current label range and a soil-specific trial.
process: Track water and solution temperature, concentration, wet dwell, flow or brush action, rinse volume, return conductivity, and dry/inspection time.
boundary: Separate raw and ready-to-eat zones, protect feed and food, follow allergen/biosecurity controls, and confirm food-contact rinse requirements.
verification: Visual release plus the site's ATP, protein/allergen, or microbiological criterion; cleaning alone does not establish sanitation.
materials: Stainless steel, food-grade polymers, belts, hoses, seals, galvanized or painted equipment, concrete, and aluminum where approved
wastewater: Screen solids and manage pH, nutrients, fats/oils/grease, and hydraulic load under the plant or farm discharge plan.

label: Golf Courses
lead_task: Clean carts, turf equipment, irrigation assets, clubhouse surfaces, and hardscape without turning runoff into a turf problem.
asset: Carts, mowers, utility vehicles, irrigation heads, pump components, shop floors, locker rooms, pavers, and fountains
soil: Grass oil, grease, fertilizer salt, mineral scale, algae staining, mud, and tracked organic soil
method: Asset-specific wash, degrease, descale, or spray-and-dwell treatment with runoff protection
concentration: Set each task within the current product label/TDS range; start weak near painted equipment, turf, water features, and irrigation elastomers.
process: Record surface temperature, dilution, dwell, brush/low-pressure action, rinse requirement, and dry or return-to-play time.
boundary: Protect turf, ponds, irrigation intakes, players, and battery/electrical components; separate cleaning from antimicrobial treatment.
verification: Dry visual acceptance, no oily or slippery film, restored nozzle flow where relevant, and no visible turf or finish impact after the test area.
materials: Painted steel, aluminum, plastics, vinyl, rubber, concrete, pavers, irrigation polymers, and planted turf
wastewater: Wash equipment at the designated pad; capture oil and solids and prevent cleaning solution from entering ponds or storm drains.

label: Golf Courses & Sports Facilities
lead_task: Clean grounds equipment, irrigation, athletic hardscape, locker rooms, and carts around active turf and public schedules.
asset: Mowers, carts, irrigation hardware, stadium hardscape, locker-room floors, pool or fountain components, and maintenance shops
soil: Turf oil, grease, rubber transfer, body-soil film, fertilizer mineral, algae staining, and hard-water scale
method: Segmented equipment wash, low-foam surface cleaning, targeted descaling, and label-directed exterior treatment
concentration: Use the weakest current-label dilution that passes surface, turf-edge, and slip-residue tests; keep separate ratios by task.
process: Log dilution, surface temperature, dwell, pad/brush or spray action, rinse, ventilation, and dry-to-use time.
boundary: Close the work zone, protect athletes and guests, isolate irrigation and electrical assets, and keep facility disinfection under its approved program.
verification: No visible film, acceptable slip condition, same-angle dry photos, restored irrigation flow when targeted, and no turf-edge injury.
materials: Sport flooring, sealed concrete, painted metal, aluminum, plastics, rubber, tile, grout, irrigation polymers, and turf
wastewater: Use designated wash pads and floor drains; intercept solids/oil and keep runoff out of playing fields and surface water.

label: Healthcare
lead_task: Clean isolated mechanical and facility assets without crossing infection-control, occupied-care, or water-management boundaries.
asset: Cooling towers, closed loops, heat exchangers, steam-plant equipment, kitchen/laundry equipment, drains, and nonclinical hard surfaces
soil: Scale, rust, corrosion product, grease, soap film, mineral deposit, and ordinary facility soil
method: Permit-controlled water-side cleaning or zone-specific facility cleaning followed by the facility's required disinfection step
concentration: Set descaling concentration from the current label/user guide, deposit analysis, and metallurgy; all treatment dosing remains under the facility water plan.
process: Record temperature, concentration, flow/agitation, contact time, rinse pH/conductivity, ventilation, barricade, and restart readings.
boundary: Use infection-control risk assessment, LOTO, ASHRAE 188/water-management controls, and facility-approved disinfectants. Cleaning is not disinfection.
verification: Mechanical trend recovery plus neutral/stable rinse; environmental ATP or microbiological release only when required and interpreted by the facility.
materials: Copper, stainless and carbon steel, aluminum, elastomers, coated tower parts, tile, sealed flooring, and approved polymers
wastewater: Characterize pH, metals, and biocide/treatment residuals; route under hospital EHS and wastewater authorization.

label: Healthcare & Senior Living
lead_task: Remove grease, scale, and ordinary soil in resident-facing facilities before the approved infection-prevention step.
asset: Kitchens, laundries, mechanical rooms, restroom fixtures, nonclinical floors, drains, carts, and isolated heat-transfer equipment
soil: Cooking grease, laundry film, soap scum, hard-water scale, tracked soil, and drain residue
method: Low-odor zone cleaning, controlled dwell and agitation, full recovery/rinse, then facility-approved disinfection where required
concentration: Use the lowest current-label dilution that passes a finish and residue test; descaling ratios require fixture metallurgy and deposit review.
process: Document dilution, surface temperature, wet dwell, agitation, rinse/recovery, ventilation, dry time, and reoccupancy release.
boundary: Coordinate infection prevention, resident protection, food service, ventilation, fall prevention, and chemical storage. No disinfectant claim is borrowed.
verification: No visible soil or film, dry white-wipe, acceptable slip condition, rinse baseline for descaling, then the facility's separate hygiene endpoint.
materials: Resilient flooring, tile, grout, stainless steel, copper, chrome, plastics, sealed stone, painted surfaces, and elastomers
wastewater: Route grease through interceptors and descaling solution under facility pH/discharge limits; never use resident-area storm drains.

label: Hotels / Property Management
lead_task: Remove grease, soap film, mineral scale, and exterior staining while guest-facing areas remain controlled and presentable.
asset: Commercial kitchens, laundry equipment, restroom fixtures, mechanical rooms, pool-side hardscape, façades, drains, and parking surfaces
soil: Cooking grease, soap scum, carbonate scale, body-soil film, algae staining, tire marks, and atmospheric grime
method: Zone-specific degreasing, descaling, surface washing, or label-directed spray-and-dwell treatment
concentration: Use the weakest current-label dilution that removes the target soil after a hidden-area finish, grout, sealant, and slip-residue test.
process: Record dilution, surface temperature, dwell, agitation, rinse/recovery, ventilation, odor check, dry time, and area release.
boundary: Barricade guest traffic, protect food/pools/landscaping, follow finish warranties, and keep cleaning separate from pool treatment and disinfection.
verification: Dry visual and white-wipe acceptance, no streak or slippery film, neutral rinse where applicable, and no finish change in the test area.
materials: Tile, grout, stone, stainless steel, chrome, glass, sealed concrete, paint, roofing, plastics, and landscaping
wastewater: Use kitchen interceptors and approved sanitary drains; block storm inlets and protect pool and landscape water.

label: Hotels, Resorts & Property Management
lead_task: Standardize guest-area, back-of-house, and exterior cleaning by soil, surface, and operating window.
asset: Guest and public hard surfaces, kitchens, laundry, mechanical equipment, pool decks, façades, roofs, drains, and fleet carts
soil: Grease, soap and body-soil film, scale, algae staining, food residue, tire marks, and atmospheric deposit
method: Tested zone-specific cleaning with low-odor application, controlled dwell, recovery/rinse, and dry release
concentration: Keep a documented current-label range by task and use the weakest effective starting dilution for each guest-facing finish.
process: Log dilution, temperature, dwell, agitation, rinse/recovery, ventilation, odor, drying, and reopening time.
boundary: Coordinate guest access, housekeeping, food service, pool operations, landscaping, and surface warranties; no cleaning-disinfection substitution.
verification: No visible soil or residue, acceptable dry slip condition, finish/gloss acceptance, and manager sign-off before reopening.
materials: Stone, tile, grout, resilient flooring, stainless steel, glass, paint, roofing, concrete, plastics, and textiles kept out of scope
wastewater: Route by soil source through interceptor or sanitary systems; contain exterior runoff away from pools, beaches, and stormwater.

label: HVAC / Water Treatment
lead_task: Remove water-side scale and corrosion product, then return the isolated system to a documented treatment program.
asset: Cooling towers, fill, plate and shell heat exchangers, condensers, boilers, closed loops, coils, strainers, and piping
soil: Calcium carbonate, iron oxide, mixed mineral scale, silt, corrosion product, and organic fouling
method: Isolate, circulate or soak descaler, monitor reaction, drain, rinse, inspect, and recommission treatment
concentration: Select within the current HCR/user-guide range from deposit loading, metallurgy, volume, and reaction monitoring; treatment dose is site-engineered.
process: Track concentration, solution temperature, flow/agitation, pH trend, iron/hardness response, dwell, rinse conductivity, and restart chemistry.
boundary: Use LOTO, bypass controls, ventilation, Legionella/water-management procedures, metallurgy checks, and treatment-vendor approval.
verification: Improved approach temperature, flow, or pressure drop; stable rinse pH/conductivity; clean inspection point; treatment residual back in range.
materials: Copper, carbon steel, stainless steel, aluminum, galvanized steel, tower polymers, elastomers, and treatment sensors
wastewater: Characterize spent solution for pH and metals; neutralize and discharge only through the approved facility route.

label: Manufacturing
lead_task: Remove process oil, carbon, grease, and scale from isolated production assets with a measurable return-to-process endpoint.
asset: Parts, machine tools, floors, conveyors, tanks, heat exchangers, molds, dies, and utility piping
soil: Cutting oil, hydraulic fluid, grease, carbonized residue, adhesive film, rust, and mineral scale
method: Parts wash, controlled foam/spray, manual agitation, or isolated circulation selected by asset and soil
concentration: Use the current label/TDS range and establish the weakest effective starting point through a material coupon and soil-loading trial.
process: Record bath/surface temperature, concentration, dwell, spray/brush/flow agitation, rinse quality, dry time, and bath-loading limits.
boundary: LOTO and de-inventory equipment, verify coatings/seals/metallurgy, protect controls and bearings, and segregate incompatible waste streams.
verification: Water-break or white-wipe acceptance where appropriate, specified surface energy/cleanliness, restored flow or pressure drop, and no corrosion/finish change.
materials: Carbon and stainless steel, aluminum, copper, engineered polymers, elastomers, paint, powder coat, and conversion coatings
wastewater: Profile oil, metals, pH, and solids; use oil-water separation or hazardous/industrial waste routes defined by the plant.

label: Marine
lead_task: Remove salt, marine film, oil, and oxidation from vessels and dockside assets without releasing an oily wash plume.
asset: Hulls, decks, topsides, bilges, engine-room surfaces, aluminum rails, trailers, dock equipment, and service floors
soil: Salt film, algae staining, diesel soot, bilge oil, grease, fish residue, road film, and aluminum oxidation
method: Fresh-water pre-rinse, targeted wash/degrease or brightening, soft agitation, complete rinse, and recovery
concentration: Keep wash and degreaser within current label ranges; establish brightener strength only after an alloy, anodizing, coating, and sealant test.
process: Record panel temperature, salinity of rinse water, dilution, dwell, brush/low-pressure action, rinse volume, and dry inspection.
boundary: Protect antifouling and specialty coatings, electrical systems, bilges, zincs, glazing, and adjacent water; follow marina and vessel OEM rules.
verification: No salt or oily film after dry, no gloss/coating change, clean white-wipe at the test area, and no visible sheen in recovered water.
materials: Gelcoat, painted steel, aluminum, stainless steel, teak kept out unless approved, vinyl, rubber, glass, and marine sealants
wastewater: Use a contained wash pad or mobile recovery; separate oil and solids and never discharge cleaning solution directly to surface water.

label: Marine, Marinas & Boatyards
lead_task: Clean vessel exteriors, service bays, bilges, and aluminum components inside a marina or boatyard wash-water plan.
asset: Hull and topside surfaces, decks, bilges, engine bays, lifts, trailers, aluminum rails, docks, and service floors
soil: Salt, algae staining, oil and grease, diesel soot, fish residue, road film, and aluminum oxidation
method: Fresh-water rinse, task-specific wash/degrease, controlled brightening where approved, recovery, and dry inspection
concentration: Use the current wash or descaler label range; determine any aluminum-brightening ratio on a hidden alloy/finish coupon first.
process: Document surface temperature, dilution, dwell, agitation, rinse volume, recovery, and dry finish condition.
boundary: Confirm coating and alloy, isolate shore power, protect bilges and water, and comply with yard permits and vessel-owner authorization.
verification: Dry no-film inspection, gloss/finish acceptance, white-wipe where practical, and zero visible sheen outside containment.
materials: Gelcoat, marine paint, aluminum, stainless steel, vinyl, rubber, glass, sealants, and antifouling systems
wastewater: Capture at the work area; route through yard solids/oil controls and the authorized sanitary or waste-hauler path.

label: Mechanical Contractors & Water Treatment
lead_task: Descale isolated boilers, heat exchangers, coils, and water loops with a documented handoff back to treatment.
asset: Plate and shell heat exchangers, boilers, cooling towers, coils, pumps, closed loops, strainers, and temporary circulation rigs
soil: Carbonate and mixed mineral scale, iron oxide, corrosion product, silt, and water-side organic film
method: LOTO, isolate, establish temporary circulation, monitor descaling, drain, rinse, inspect, and recommission
concentration: Choose within the current HCR/Descaler guide from deposit, metallurgy, loop volume, and reaction rate; do not use a universal ratio.
process: Log flow, solution temperature, concentration, pH/reaction trend, dwell, iron/hardness response, rinse conductivity, and restart chemistry.
boundary: Written method statement, LOTO, pressure relief, venting, hose/rig compatibility, spill containment, owner approval, and Legionella controls.
verification: Recovered flow, pressure drop, or approach temperature; stable rinse baseline; clean inspection point; treatment residual restored.
materials: Copper, carbon and stainless steel, aluminum, galvanized steel, elastomers, brazing alloys, plastics, and sensors
wastewater: Characterize pH and dissolved metals; neutralize and route through the owner's authorized discharge or waste-hauler process.

label: Military / Government
lead_task: Clean fleet, facility, and utility assets under technical-order, procurement, and chain-of-custody controls.
asset: Motor-pool vehicles, ground equipment, hangar floors, public works machinery, heat exchangers, water assets, and maintenance shops
soil: Petroleum grease, hydraulic oil, carbon, road film, rust, mineral scale, and ordinary facility soil
method: Approved work-card degreasing, parts cleaning, floor recovery, or isolated descaling with documented lot and operator data
concentration: Use only current controlled label/TDS ranges and the task order's approved starting dilution after material and process review.
process: Record product lot, dilution, temperature, dwell, agitation/flow, rinse, waste volume, inspection result, and return-to-service authorization.
boundary: Follow technical orders, SDS approval, LOTO, environmental plan, security/access rules, material authorization, and contract scope.
verification: Work-card inspection criterion, white-wipe/water-break where specified, mechanical performance endpoint, and signed chain-of-custody record.
materials: Painted and bare metals, aluminum, stainless steel, composites, elastomers, concrete, coatings, and government-specified materials
wastewater: Profile and containerize by installation rules; use approved separators, industrial discharge, or waste contracts.

label: Municipalities & Water Utilities
lead_task: Remove scale, rust, and grease from isolated utility assets without confusing cleaning with potable-water disinfection.
asset: Pumps, valves, screens, strainers, heat exchangers, treatment skids, maintenance floors, and out-of-service storage components
soil: Carbonate scale, iron and manganese deposit, rust, grease, silt, and treatment-chemical residue
method: Isolate, mechanically remove bulk soil, circulate or soak cleaner, agitate, drain, rinse, inspect, and return under utility procedure
concentration: Set cleaning concentration from the current label/user guide, deposit sample, metallurgy, and asset volume; treatment dosing is utility-engineered.
process: Track concentration, solution temperature, flow/agitation, pH, dwell, metal response, rinse conductivity/turbidity, and controlled restart.
boundary: Use LOTO, confined-space rules, cross-connection control, permit requirements, and the utility's separate disinfection and sampling plan for potable assets.
verification: Clean inspection point, restored flow or pressure drop, stable rinse pH/conductivity/turbidity, then required utility bacteriological release.
materials: Ductile iron, carbon and stainless steel, copper, concrete, coatings, PVC/HDPE, elastomers, and treatment instruments
wastewater: Characterize pH, metals, solids, and treatment residuals; route only under the utility's NPDES, sewer, or hauled-waste authorization.

label: Oil & Gas
lead_task: Remove hydrocarbon soil and mineral deposit from de-inventoried rigs, terminals, and process-support assets.
asset: Tanks, heat exchangers, separators, pipe spools, pumps, valves, rig equipment, containment floors, and vehicle components
soil: Crude and refined hydrocarbon film, grease, drilling residue, carbon, iron oxide, carbonate scale, and mixed deposits
method: De-inventory and gas-free, remove bulk product, controlled degrease or circulate descaler, recover, rinse, and inspect
concentration: Select within the current label/TDS range from deposit analysis, metallurgy, soil load, and a contained field trial.
process: Log LEL/O2 status, solution temperature, concentration, dwell, flow or mechanical agitation, rinse/recovery volume, pH, and waste profile.
boundary: Permit to work, LOTO/blinding, gas testing, confined-space control, ignition control, materials review, and spill containment are prerequisites.
verification: Gas-free status maintained, no visible/free oil, white-wipe or specified cleanliness, recovered flow/pressure drop, and acceptable rinse endpoint.
materials: Carbon and stainless steel, specialty alloys, coatings/linings, elastomers, FRP, concrete, and instrument components
wastewater: Profile hydrocarbons, metals, pH, and solids; route to the site's oily-water treatment or licensed waste stream.

label: Oil & Gas / Industrial Plants
lead_task: Clean hydrocarbon, grease, and scale from isolated process and utility assets under plant permit controls.
asset: Tanks, exchangers, separators, process piping, pumps, valves, equipment skids, shop parts, and containment floors
soil: Oil and grease, hydrocarbon sludge, carbon, corrosion product, carbonate scale, and mixed process deposit
method: Decontaminate and isolate, bulk-remove, degrease or circulate, recover, rinse, inspect, and document waste
concentration: Use the applicable current label/TDS range; set the trial point from soil/deposit analysis, metallurgy, temperature, and circulation capability.
process: Record gas test, concentration, temperature, wet dwell, spray/brush/flow agitation, rinse, recovery, and waste characterization.
boundary: Permit, LOTO/blinding, confined-space and gas-free controls, ignition management, process-owner approval, and compatible temporary equipment.
verification: No free hydrocarbon, defined white-wipe/visual criterion, stable rinse endpoint, recovered thermal/hydraulic performance, and signed acceptance.
materials: Carbon and stainless steel, alloys, linings, FRP, elastomers, concrete, paint, and instrumentation
wastewater: Segregate oily and scale-bearing streams; profile before oily-water treatment, reuse, or licensed disposal.

label: Plumbing
lead_task: Restore flow and heat transfer in isolated tankless heaters, boilers, fixtures, and scale-prone water components.
asset: Tankless heat exchangers, boilers, recirculation components, valves, fixtures, strainers, pumps, and service piping
soil: Calcium carbonate, mixed mineral scale, rust, iron deposit, and soap/mineral film
method: Isolate, establish service circulation or controlled soak, monitor descaling, drain, rinse, and restore per OEM procedure
concentration: Choose within the current HCR/Descaler guide from scale severity, metallurgy, water volume, and OEM limits; no universal ratio.
process: Log solution temperature, concentration, circulation flow, pH/reaction trend, dwell, rinse pH/conductivity, and post-service flow.
boundary: Use LOTO and pressure relief, protect potable cross-connections, confirm metals/elastomers, follow OEM warranty, and fully flush before service.
verification: Recovered flow or temperature rise, clean inspection point/strainer, stable rinse pH/conductivity, leak check, and potable return-to-service procedure.
materials: Copper, stainless steel, brass, nickel alloys, aluminum where approved, PVC/CPVC, PEX kept isolated as required, and elastomers
wastewater: Neutralize if required and discharge only under local plumbing/sewer rules; capture metal-rich or prohibited waste.

label: Pressure-Washing & Soft-Wash Contractors
lead_task: Remove algae staining, atmospheric soil, and traffic film from exteriors with pressure matched to the substrate.
asset: Roofs, siding, stucco, painted masonry, concrete, pavers, fences, storefronts, and exterior glass
soil: Algae, lichen and mildew staining, soot, pollen, bird residue, tire marks, oil spots, and general grime
method: Pre-wet/protect, apply tested soft-wash or cleaner, control dwell, agitate only as needed, then rinse/recover per label
concentration: Use the weakest current-label dilution that clears the test area; never increase chemistry or pressure before checking dwell and coverage.
process: Record weather, surface temperature, dilution, nozzle pressure/flow, dwell, agitation, rinse volume, and dry inspection.
boundary: Protect plants, occupants, coatings, sealants, electrical entries, neighboring property, and storm drains; observe ladder and work-at-height controls.
verification: Matched-angle dry photos, no streak or residue, finish/color acceptance, and no plant or runoff impact after the trial area.
materials: Roofing, vinyl, stucco, painted masonry, concrete, pavers, wood only if approved, glass, sealants, and landscaping
wastewater: Block storm inlets, recover oily/chemical wash water, and follow local mobile-wash and property discharge rules.

label: Restaurants & Commercial Kitchens
lead_task: Remove polymerized fat, grease, and carbon from kitchen assets before the required rinse and sanitation step.
asset: Hoods, filters, fryers kept out unless OEM-approved, floors, walls, equipment exteriors, grease traps, drains, and wash areas
soil: Animal and vegetable fat, polymerized grease, carbonized food, protein film, floor oil, and drain residue
method: Cool and isolate, scrape bulk soil, apply degreaser, control dwell, brush/foam, hot rinse where allowed, and recover
concentration: Use the current CR HD/MultiWash label range; start at the weakest dilution that passes stainless, aluminum, grout, and slip-residue tests.
process: Record surface and solution temperature, dilution, dwell, foam/brush action, rinse temperature/volume, recovery, and dry time.
boundary: Shut down heat and ignition, protect food, isolate hood fire systems as authorized, verify aluminum, and keep cleaning separate from sanitizing.
verification: No visible grease, clean white cloth, no slippery film after dry, clear drain flow, then the kitchen's separate sanitation release.
materials: Stainless steel, aluminum only after test, tile, grout, sealed flooring, plastics, rubber, paint, and hood components
wastewater: Scrape solids first; route fats/oils/grease through the interceptor and approved sanitary drain, never stormwater.

label: Schools & Universities
lead_task: Clean campus plumbing, HVAC, kitchen, restroom, gym, and exterior assets within district approval and occupancy controls.
asset: Heat exchangers, coils, fixtures, kitchens, restroom and gym floors, drains, maintenance equipment, façades, and hardscape
soil: Scale, rust, grease, soap film, tracked dirt, rubber transfer, algae staining, and ordinary facility residue
method: Off-hour zone-specific descaling, degreasing, surface cleaning, and complete rinse/recovery
concentration: Use the applicable current label range and approve a weakest-effective starting dilution through facilities/EHS and a small-area trial.
process: Log dilution, surface/solution temperature, dwell, agitation, rinse/recovery, ventilation, barricade, dry time, and reopening.
boundary: Protect students and staff, isolate ventilation/traffic, coordinate food service and athletics, and use separate district-approved disinfectants.
verification: No visible film, dry white-wipe, acceptable slip condition, neutral/stable rinse for descaling, and facilities sign-off.
materials: Stainless steel, copper, aluminum, resilient and sport flooring, tile, grout, concrete, paint, plastics, and elastomers
wastewater: Route grease, floor solution, and scale-bearing cleanout through district-approved pretreatment and sanitary systems.

label: Solar / Panel Cleaning
lead_task: Remove dust, bird residue, salt, and mineral spotting from modules without abrading glass or compromising energized equipment.
asset: Photovoltaic module glass, frames, clamps, trackers, inverter-pad hardscape, and accessible support structures
soil: Dust, pollen, bird residue, salt film, industrial fallout, light organic film, and hard-water spotting
method: Deionized or low-mineral pre-rinse, approved low-residue cleaner, soft brush/pad, and spot-free rinse
concentration: Use the weakest current-label dilution that passes the module maker's coating and residue test; water-only remains the baseline where OEM-required.
process: Record irradiance/weather, glass temperature, water conductivity, dilution, dwell, brush pressure, rinse volume, and drying condition.
boundary: Follow module/O&M warranty, energized-work, fall, tracker, coating, and electrical-connector restrictions; avoid thermal shock and dry cleaning abrasion.
verification: Spot-free dry glass, matched-angle imaging, no coating/scratch change, and normalized before/after power or soiling-ratio trend when available.
materials: Tempered coated glass, anodized aluminum, sealants, backsheet edges, cable jackets, plastics, and painted/galvanized supports
wastewater: Map runoff, protect soil and waterways, and capture chemical or contaminated rinse where the site permit requires it.

label: Solar Farms & Panel Cleaning
lead_task: Clean utility-scale modules by soiling zone while protecting coatings, trackers, electrical gear, and site drainage.
asset: Module glass, frames, trackers, row hardware, weather stations, and inverter-area hardscape
soil: Dust, clay, pollen, bird residue, salt, agricultural film, industrial fallout, and mineral spotting
method: Zone trial, low-mineral rinse, OEM-approved low-residue chemistry where needed, soft agitation, and controlled dry
concentration: Start with water; if chemistry is approved, use the weakest current-label dilution that passes module coating and residue checks.
process: Log row/zone, glass temperature, irradiance, water conductivity, dilution, dwell, brush pressure, rinse volume, weather, and dry condition.
boundary: Use site electrical and tracker procedures, module warranties, work-at-height/vehicle controls, vegetation protection, and weather limits.
verification: Spot-free dry inspection, no scratches/coating change, repeatable images, and normalized soiling or power trend against an untreated control.
materials: Coated tempered glass, anodized aluminum, sealants, cable jackets, backsheets, tracker coatings, and galvanized steel
wastewater: Prevent ponding and offsite flow; route chemically assisted or contaminant-bearing rinse under the solar site's drainage plan.

label: Warehousing & Distribution Centers
lead_task: Remove oil, tire marks, and pallet grime from floors, docks, and material-handling equipment without leaving residue.
asset: Concrete and coated floors, docks, forklifts, pallet jacks, racks, battery areas, shop parts, and drains
soil: Hydraulic oil, grease, tire polymer, battery-area residue kept segregated, cardboard dust, adhesive, and tracked grime
method: Sweep, spot-treat, low-foam auto-scrub or controlled degrease, recover, rinse, and dry
concentration: Use the current label range and establish the weakest effective auto-scrubber or spot-treatment dilution by floor/coating zone.
process: Record floor temperature, dilution, dwell, pad/brush choice, scrub/recovery passes, rinse, and dry-to-traffic time.
boundary: Isolate traffic and powered equipment, segregate food/packaging, protect rack coatings and battery systems, and control slip risk.
verification: No visible oil or tire film, dry white-wipe, facility slip-resistance acceptance, and no foam/residue after the recovery pass.
materials: Polished or sealed concrete, epoxy/urethane coatings, painted steel, aluminum, rubber tires, plastics, and drain components
wastewater: Recover scrubber solution; separate oil and solids and route through the facility's approved pretreatment/discharge system.
